title: Ontario permit-to-start-to-completion conversion evidence
question: Which permit intentions become starts, completions, and occupancy?
why_it_matters: Building permits are upstream intentions. FTFN needs conversion evidence to know whether approvals become starts, completions, occupied units, or stalled projects.
current_support: FTFN has Statistics Canada permits, CMHC starts and completions data, a June 2026 CMHC Toronto CMA baseline separating approved units awaiting starts, units under construction, completions, and starts, Toronto's 2025 Development Pipeline, application 24 254930 records showing movement from initial notice through staff review to a July 2026 committee recommendation, and a full-address Building Permit portal recheck.
missing_evidence: building permit and permit-to-start conversion for application 24 254930
candidate_records: specific Toronto building permit for application 24 254930
application 24 254930 start, completion, and occupancy record
next_action: Keep CMHC's metropolitan stage stocks and flows separate and do not calculate an unmatched conversion rate. Recheck the Council and bill trail after July 29-31, then search the Building Permit portal with a confirmed application number or later project record and track construction start, completion, and occupancy.

named_records: CMHC June 2026 Housing Starts And Construction Data
City of Toronto Building Application Status portal
Toronto City Council item 2026.SC33.9 for application 24 254930
latest_review.stage_result: The new CMHC record distinguishes current Toronto CMA stage stocks and flows, narrowing what an aggregate conversion baseline can show. It still supplies no matched project cohort, and the selected application remains upstream of a verified Council disposition and building permit.
latest_review.stop_rule: Do not divide approved-not-started stock by monthly starts or completions, and do not infer a project permit from an address search. Reopen the named project only after the Council trail changes or a confirmed permit, start, completion, or occupancy record appears.

notes: Phase 55Q narrows the aggregate-data question and preserves the project boundary. The earlier eight address searches returned Application Not Found, but those bounded negative queries do not prove that no permit exists.
